mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registrar in the partner's country of origin (e.g., Companies House, SAMR, Secretary of State)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney executed by each proposed partner and ultimate beneficial owner appointing the Quebec filing agent / attorney-in-fact
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or required notarial authority in the signatory's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of residential address for each general partner, limited partner, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country public authority or certified notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming the source of funds and financial standing of the prospective partners and beneficial owners

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if required; otherwise consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all partners, directors, officers, attorneys-in-fact, and 25%+ ultimate beneficial owners against the FINTRAC Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) and Heads of International Organizations list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the Canadian Economic Sanctions list (Global Affairs Canada), and the U.S. OFAC SDN list for all USD payment rails. Enhanced due diligence and periodic re-screening are required if any party holds political exposure, resides in a high-risk jurisdiction, or engages in transactions using convertible virtual currency.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Online Name Reservation and Search Service (leregistre.req.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, the legal name of a Quebec enterprise must be in French. The registered name must contain a French generic or descriptor, and the legal form suffix for a limited partnership must appear in French as 'Société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.' A foreign trademark or distinctive proper noun may be incorporated only where accompanied by a French generic element or otherwise authorized by the Registrar.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name refusal, the applicant may file a request for administrative review with the Director of Legal Enterprises under section 28 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises within 30 days of receipt of the refusal. The Registrar must reconsider the application and issue a written decision. If the refusal is upheld, the applicant may appeal to the Court of Québec within 60 days of the reconsideration decision, serving all interested parties and complying with the Code of Civil Procedure rules on contested applications.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only where the provider maintains a physical, manned address in Quebec that is available for service of process, written communications, and statutory record inspection. A bare mailbox or a non-staffed forwarding address is not acceptable. For the digital ASO/SEO agency industry, which holds no statutory licensing requirement and is classified as Low_Risk_Standard, a compliant virtual office is generally sufficient to meet registered office requirements; however, the Registraire des entreprises may require disclosure that the office is a virtual establishment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated below 5% within the first year of registration for a low-risk professional services entity with no regulated activities; probability increases moderately if official records identify a virtual office without substantive business premises).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, Book V, Title 17, Chapter III — Limited Partnership (arts. 2236-2266); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1), ss. 20, 24 and 25; Regulation respecting the register of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 1).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership (Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite) filed electronically through the Registraire's online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a société en commandite. Contributions are fixed in the limited partnership agreement and may consist of money or property; a limited partner may not contribute skill or services (art. 2243 CCQ). No escrow account is required for this office-based services partnership.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolved in writing by the corporate general partner of QC App Growth LP (the "Partnership"): (1) The Partnership is formed as a limited partnership (société en commandite) under arts. 2236-2266 of the Civil Code of Québec, and the Limited Partnership Agreement is adopted. (2) The capital subscriptions set forth in the Agreement are accepted, and each limited partner shall fund its contribution as scheduled. (3) The registered office is fixed at 1200 McGill College Avenue, Montreal, and the Registraire des entreprises du Québec is appointed for service of notice. (4) The general partner's officers are authorized to make all filings, open corporate and payment accounts, and issue invoices. (5) All acts done in furtherance of this resolution are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online name reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary availability search of the proposed corporate name on the Registraire's online portal. Submit a name reservation request choosing the juridical form 'société en commandite' and include the mandatory suffix 'L.P.' or 'S.E.C.' The reservation, once granted, is valid for 60 days and must be renewed if registration is not completed within that period.
required_dossiers: Proposed name in Latin characters with mandatory 'L.P./S.E.C.' suffix
Brief statement of the partnership's main activities
Applicant general partner's contact information and NEQ if already registered
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a second reservation with a distinguishing element or submit a request for review (demande de révision) to the Registraire within the statutory delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Qualified legal counsel or notary in Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a written limited partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite) defining the general partners (commandités), limited partners (commanditaires), capital contributions, profit and loss sharing, management authority, admission and withdrawal provisions, and the registered office in Quebec. Notarization is recommended to facilitate third-party dealings but is not mandatory for registration.
required_dossiers: Identification of each general partner (individual: full name, date of birth, domicile; legal person: name and NEQ)
Identification of each limited partner and schedule of capital contributions
Written consent of the general partner accepting appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire queries the agreement or the partners' capacity, amend and re-execute the agreement with all partners' signatures; a notarized attestation may be filed to cure evidentiary defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Limited Partnership with the Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online filing service (Québec Business Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file the Declaration of Registration (déclaration d'immatriculation) online, selecting 'société en commandite'. Enter the partnership's name, registered office address in Quebec, general partner details, principal activities, and information on the partnership agreement. Pay the filing fee by credit card or electronic transfer and obtain the enterprise number (NEQ).
required_dossiers: Copy of the limited partnership agreement (available upon request)
Electronic signature authorization of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the Registraire's request for additional information (demande de renseignements complémentaires) within 15 days, or file a corrective declaration through the online self-service module.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registrations with Revenu Québec and the Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (TVQ and payroll) and Canada Revenue Agency (GST/HST Business Number)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ issued at registration, register the limited partnership for the Québec Sales Tax (TVQ) and, if employees are anticipated, for source deductions and workplace insurance. Apply for a separate GST/HST Business Number (BN) with the CRA using the partnership's name and address. The limited partnership is a pass-through entity; registrations are made in the partnership's name with the general partner as the responsible representative.
required_dossiers: General partner's identification and Canadian residency/residence information
Projected revenue and employee payroll information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a registration is delayed or rejected, reconcile the file through Revenu Québec's 'Mon dossier d'entreprise' or the CRA Business Account; provide corrected partnership agreements and general partner identification to support reactivation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank and Payment Rails Activation and Continuing Governance Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial institutions, Wise B2B, Payoneer; Registraire des entreprises for the annual declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the general partner resolution, the NEQ certificate, and proof of registered office address to open a business bank account and activate Wise B2B/Payoneer payment rails. Maintain the partnership register and prepare the annual declaration (déclaration annuelle) to the Registraire, which must be filed in the partnership's anniversary month every year. The general partner should also adopt internal procedures for invoicing, expense allocation, and tax information returns (T5013).
required_dossiers: General partner resolution authorizing bank and payment accounts
Registered office proof (lease or utility statement)
NEQ certificate and GST/TVQ registration confirmations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or payment provider rejects the KYC documentation, resubmit corrected partnership agreement extracts and updated NEQ attestation; if the annual declaration is missed, file it late and apply to the Registraire for cancellation or reduction of the late penalty by showing due diligence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None applicable — office-based advertising, app store optimization and SEO localization services (ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810) are not subject to any industrial permit in Quebec.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required; enterprise registration under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises constitutes the sole regulatory authorization for this professional services activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no Environmental Impact Assessment required; the activity generates no industrial effluent, atmospheric emissions or hazardous waste from a leased office premise.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to office operations; where applicable, electronic waste must be managed under the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of products (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 25) and municipal waste management bylaws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for standard office tenancy: fire safety certification follows the Building Act and Fire Safety Code issued by the local fire safety service; occupational health and safety compliance is registered with the CNESST under the Act respecting occupational health and safety. No special civil defense or police clearance applies to this service business.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – federal Business Number (BN) and GST/HST program administered via My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html); Revenu Québec – QST, QPIP/CNT and payroll accounts administered via Mon dossier d'entreprise/ClicSÉQUR portal (https://www.revenuquebec.ca); Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar) for the limited partnership's NEQ (Québec Enterprise Number).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Constitute the CA_LP under Quebec partnership law and register it at the Registraire des entreprises (attorney-in-fact/service agent for foreign non-resident partners), obtaining the NEQ. Step 2: Apply online to CRA for a BN with GST/HST account (Form RC1/RC1A where application by mail) and, if applicable, payroll/mport accounts. Step 3: Register with Revenu Québec via ClicSÉQUR for the QST account using the federal BN as base identifier. Step 4: Because the LP is fiscally transparent, no income tax account is opened for the partnership itself; instead the LP files the annual partnership information returns (federal T5013; Quebec TP-600) and issues T5013/TP-600 slips to each partner. Step 5: Non-resident general partners must obtain a Canadian NR account number (BN-15) to file non-resident tax returns and to support treaty relief claims.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canadian law does not provide a U.S.-style 'check-the-box' election; entity classification follows the Quebec Civil Code/Income Tax Act s. 96 partnership rules. Available elections include: (i) a partnership fiscal-period election under ITA s. 249.1(7) to adopt a non-calendar year-end where all members agree; (ii) the s. 97(2) ITA election permitting tax-deferred transfer of contributed IP/ad-tech contracts into the LP; (iii) the CRA 'small supplier' voluntary registration election for GST/HST and QST (ETA s. 240(1); Quebec QST Act equivalents), permitting the LP to register before the CAD 30,000 threshold and claim refundable ITCs; and (iv) OECD BEPS hybrid-mismatch compliance — imported hybrid and reverse-hybrid structures are subject to ITA ss. 18.2/18.3 (in force July 2022), under which foreign partners may elect to align substantive characterization to avoid deducted-but-not-included (D/NI) outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax, Taxe de vente du Québec)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual worldwide taxable supplies (the 'small supplier' threshold) — mandatory GST/HST registration once exceeded (ETA s. 240(1)); an identical CAD 30,000 threshold applies to QST (Quebec Taxation Act); voluntary registration available before the threshold to recover input tax credits; supply-based registration requirements apply, not asset-based tests; for a foreign-owned LP, the threshold is measured by the global turnover of the person and related entities, requiring careful aggregation analysis.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, no API-based Continuous Transaction Control, and no digital stamping are mandated federally or in Quebec. Invoices issued by the LP must contain: supplier name and BN/GST-HST registration number, date, description, consideration, and applicable taxes. CRA encourages but does not require PEPPOL e-invoicing. Revenu Québec's QTIP (Québec Tax Information Platform) reporting obligations apply only to digital platform operators settling gig-economy payments, not to an ASO/SEO agency's B2B cross-border invoices; records must be retained for six years from the end of the fiscal year.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: GST/HST: under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7, services supplied to a non-resident recipient are zero-rated where the recipient is not registered under the ETA and the service is not in respect of Canadian real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada. QST mirrors this result for supplies made to a non-resident not registered for QST. For the ASO/SEO localization agency: app-store optimization, multilingual keyword localization, organic search audits, metadata translations, and campaign-performance reporting supplied to non-resident app publishers qualify as zero-rated exports when the contractual recipient is outside Canada; CRA does not require preapproval, and the fact that the foreign publisher's end-users are in Canada does not by itself defeat zero-rating (CRA 'advertising services' policy). To substantiate, the LP must document the recipient's non-resident status (foreign certificate, registered office, tax ID), the exported nature of the service, and remittance from offshore accounts. Pure service exports do not require CBSA customs declarations; however, if ASO deliverables include licensed digital goods or media copyrights crossing borders, the supply is treated as intangible personal property and remains zero-rated under s. 10(2)? (intellectual property supplied to non-resident, Schedule VI Part V s. 10), for which assigned contract and license records are the primary evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / CBSA CERS record — applicable only if digital-media kits, promotional devices, or physical props are shipped; not required for pure remote services.
Bill of Lading / carrier airway bill — similarly goods-only evidence, retained if any physical deliverables are exported.
Inward remittance certificate — Wise_B2B or Payoneer payment statements, SWIFT/MT103 records, and bank credits evidencing settlement in USD/EUR from non-resident counterparties.
Executed service agreement containing governing law, Quebec/non-resident status representations, and scope-of-work defining exported services.
Commercial invoice pack stamped 'Zero-rated export — ETA Schedule VI s.7 / QST equivalent', quoting the LP's GST/HST and QST registration numbers and the recipient's foreign tax ID.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC); Minister of Finance for policy matters
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains free convertibility on both current and capital account transactions. There are no general foreign-exchange controls, no restrictions on foreign-currency deposits, and no requirement for prior exchange-control approval for inbound or outbound payments. The Bank of Canada does not impose surrender or repatriation requirements on export receipts or service revenues. Profit remittances from a Quebec Limited Partnership to non-resident partners remain subject to Canadian tax withholding under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act on taxable distributions such as interest, dividends, rents, royalties, and certain management fees; however, business income allocated to non-resident partners is generally taxed under Part I and remittance must be supported by Form NR4, fileable by the partnership or its general partner, with treaty-based rate reductions available. Payment rails must comply with money-laundering reporting thresholds under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), including FINTRAC reports for electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more in a 24-hour period.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio exists for a Quebec Limited Partnership. Export and cross-border service receipts may be retained in the original foreign currency, converted at commercial bank rates, or used directly for trade disbursements. The only obligations are: (i) accurate accounting in Canadian dollar equivalent for tax filings; (ii) reporting by a registered Canadian money services business if converting funds on behalf of third parties; and (iii) FINTRAC large-transaction and SWIFT/CAD-related transfer reporting obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (National Bank / Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium, with legal constraints. Canadian law does not recognise the European-style 'electronic money institution' designation as a chartered bank; such entities are generally treated as money services businesses (MSBs) and must register with FINTRAC if operating in or targeting Canada, appoint a chief AML officer, and implement a compliance program. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise B2B and Payoneer can be used as secondary disbursement and receivables-concentration rails, but cannot legally be the sole treasury infrastructure for a Quebec LP because they do not provide a Canadian deposit account, lack CDIC deposit insurance protection, are not licensed loan or deposit-taking corporations under the Bank Act, and may require the underlying corporate entity to maintain a separate bank account. Where the offshore EMI is itself a regulated money transmitter in its home jurisdiction, the Quebec LP should provide the EMI with tax residency evidence, ultimate beneficial owner declarations, and a copy of the limited partnership registration from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is partially permitted but materially constrained. For a Quebec Limited Partnership, FINTRAC-compliant identity verification of the general partner, all partners owning 25% or more of the partnership, and the senior managing officers is mandatory. Most Tier 1 Canadian banks require the general partner or authorised signing officer to attend an in-person or live-video-notarised verification meeting, particularly for cross-border structures without Canadian directors. Pure remote opening without any physical presence is generally unavailable for escrow or high-transaction operational accounts. Banks may accept certified copies of passports and proof of address, but will usually require wet-ink signatures, a Canadian-registered partnership number, and a notarised resolution or power of attorney signed by all general partners. The practical minimum is one physical visit by an authorised representative to the branch or a video-call KYC interview coupled with a certified true-copy package couriered from the jurisdiction of formation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited partnership structure with non-resident limited partners and no Canadian-resident general partner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bound partnership agreement; registered declaration of co-ownership or declaration of registration issued by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; register of partners and beneficial owners; ultimate beneficial ownership declaration signed by the general partner; passport, proof of address, and tax residency self-certifications for all 25%+ partners; organisational chart; business plan describing the App Store Optimization and multilingual search agency services; source of funds letters and bank references from the jurisdiction of each non-resident partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border disbursements to digital advertising platforms and overseas subcontractors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed client agreements; itemised invoices and statements for Google Ads, Apple Search Ads, and social media platforms; subcontractor agreements and vendor due diligence files; historical bank statements demonstrating consistent advertising-technology payments; invoice-to-cash-flow reconciliation; explanation of the ASO and SEO service delivery model to distinguish service payments from unrelated trade flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of Wise B2B and Payoneer as treasury rails alongside Tier 1 bank accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written FinTech usage policy; the entities' own anti-money-laundering and sanctions-screening controls; FinTRAC MSB registration certificate for any Canadian presence of the fintech provider; counterparty bank verification; regular transaction monitoring reports; evidence that the operational bank account is held at a Canadian chartered bank and that the EMI is used only for low-value operating payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrow or capital injection arriving from a tax-haven or non-OECD intermediary bank
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds letter from the sending financial institution; ultimate parent company ownership chart; audited financial statements of the investing partner; evidence of the commercial purpose of the capital injection; a closing memorandum or capital contribution resolution; transaction trail through the ordering bank with FATCA/CRS self-certification; pre-currency-conversion confirmation and purpose-code declaration.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions must be wired in the partner's local currency or Canadian dollars via SWIFT MT103 using the partnership's beneficiary institution code and Canadian bank transit/institution number. For a Canadian recipient, use the 9-digit routing numeric identifier (institution number + 5-digit branch transit) and the partnership's account number; Canada does not operate an IBAN system, so all cross-border wires require BIC/SWIFT of the receiving Canadian chartered bank. The MT103 must include a clear purpose code such as 'Capital contribution to limited partnership', 'Equity injection', or 'Foreign direct investment (FDI) inflow' as required by the receiving bank's external-payments code list. For partner contributions from the United States, the payer may use the existing USD clearing hub (Fedwire) with ABA routing through the Canadian bank's U.S. correspondent; for contributions from Europe, the sending bank will route via SWIFT with no IBAN but with full beneficiary legal name, registered address, and CA/QC partnership identifier. Verification procedures include: (i) pre-notification by the general partner; (ii) matching of the remitter information against the partnership register; (iii) source-of-funds documents; (iv) confirmation of no sanctions-prohibited jurisdictions; and (v) posting of the contribution to the partnership capital account with contemporaneous accounting entry.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlement are executed over SWIFT MT103 for international telegraphic transfers, via the Canadian Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) / Lynx high-value payment rails for cross-bank CAD settlement, and via bank-to-bank ACH or EFT for recurring CAD vendor payments. For USD payments to U.S. publishers and advertising platforms, Canadian Tier 1 banks use U.S. dollar clearing through a U.S. correspondent bank, either by Automated Clearing House (ACH) for low-value recurring settlements or Fedwire for larger or time-critical disbursements. Commercial letters of credit are technically available and appropriate for physical-goods transactions, but for an app growth and localization agency they are not the standard rail; instead, confirmed SWIFT MT103 wire transfers, commercial invoicing with credit terms, and payment platform settlement files are the primary outbound rails. All outbound transfers must include a valid transaction purpose code, such as 'Payment for digital advertising services', 'Licence fees', 'Royalties', or 'Management consulting fees', and must be screened against Canadian economic sanctions, including the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Options (vanilla call and put options)
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for restricted emerging-market currency exposures only, not for CAD because Canadian dollars are freely convertible

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) to the Registraire des entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of the limited partnership's registration in the Quebec enterprise register; if the anniversary falls on a non-business day, the next business day applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual declaration is an offence under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; monetary fines may be imposed on each of the general partners. Continued delinquency for two consecutive years permits the REQ to administratively radiate (strike off) the limited partnership after formal notice, resulting in loss of registration and legal publicity protection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 150 days after the partnership's fiscal period-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the return is due by May 31 of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a penalty of CAD 25 per day, up to CAD 2,500, calculated on each partnership non-filing; additional penalties may apply for gross negligence, repeated non-compliance, or failure to provide partner Canada Revenue Agency information slips. Persistent non-filing can trigger an arbitrary assessment and criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Partnership Register Audit and General Partner Confirmation Resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal and relevant financial institutions and auditor (not filed with a government registry unless requested)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before the REQ annual declaration deadline; the general partner must confirm the accuracy of the register of limited partners and general partners and adopt a resolution approving the annual confirmation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain and audit the statutory registers constitutes a breach of the general partner's management duties under the Civil Code of Québec; it can lead to removal by partners, personal liability for losses, and evidence of non-compliance that may be used by the Registraire to impose filing penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None by statute solely because of the limited partnership form. A mandatory independent audit is triggered only if: (i) the partnership is a reporting issuer under Canadian securities laws; (ii) the partnership agreement expressly requires an annual audit; (iii) a partner or a creditor holding at least 10% of the partnership's interests serves a written demand requiring an audit; or (iv) the Canada Revenue Agency or Revenu Québec issues a formal audit demand. For this advertising and SEO agency LP, no automatic gross-revenue or asset-threshold requires a professional audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP. Private limited partnerships ordinarily prepare financial statements using Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). IFRS is mandatory only if the LP is publicly accountable or is designated as a reporting issuer. The selected framework must be applied consistently for partnership accounting and partner reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually before filing the Déclaration annuelle with the Registraire des entreprises, the general partner must (i) review and confirm the registered data, including the identity and address of each general partner; (ii) verify the internal register of limited partners, contributions, withdrawals, and any transfer of partnership interests during the preceding fiscal year; (iii) execute a written confirmation that no undisclosed change of beneficial ownership has occurred; and (iv) update the internal beneficial ownership register where any partner holds or controls 25% or more of the partnership interests, in compliance with the federal Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 900 per year for registered office and annual agent services in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 6,500 for a typical review engagement; USD 7,500 - USD 18,000 for a full statutory audit, if required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% (combined federal 15% and Quebec provincial 11.5% general corporate rate; LP is pass-through, no entity-level tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No direct corporate tax incentives for the LP itself; partners may claim applicable deductions and credits. Quebec offers a reduced corporate rate of 5% for small businesses (first $500k) and tax credits for R&D, innovation, and export.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 (Partnership Information Return) via CRA My Business
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 5 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., May 31 for Dec 31 year-end)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all income earned in Canada; non-resident partners must report their share on their Canadian tax return.
Deductible expenses must be allocated to partners; non-resident partners must ensure expenses are reasonable and documented.
Allocate net income to partners based on partnership agreement; non-resident partners are subject to Part XIII withholding on distributions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the amount due plus 5% per month up to 12 months. For T5013, a penalty of $25 per day per partner, up to $2,500 per partner, for late filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-17 (Quebec Partnership Return) via Revenu Québec's online portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 5 months after fiscal year-end (same as federal)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report income allocated to Quebec; non-resident partners must file a Quebec tax return if they have Quebec-source income.
Claim only Quebec-specific deductions; non-residents may be subject to additional withholding.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the amount due plus 5% per month up to 12 months. Additional penalties for failure to provide information.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (statutory rate for dividends to non-residents; for partnership distributions, the same rate applies to income allocated to non-resident partners)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the non-resident partner must provide a Certificate of Residence (Form NR301) to the partnership. The partnership must submit the certificate to the CRA and withhold at the reduced treaty rate. For Quebec, a similar process applies with Revenu Québec.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25%, treaty-reduced to 10% (e.g., under US treaty) or 0% (e.g., under EU treaties). Interest: statutory 25%, treaty-reduced to 0% (e.g., US) or 10% (e.g., some treaties).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 for goods; CAD 500,000 for services, interest, royalties, and other transactions with non-resident related parties
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and requires genuine economic substance. The partnership must have real business activity, employees, and assets. No specific ESR, but substance is required to avoid GAAR.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income or overstatement of expenses in the partnership return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties: fines up to 200% of the tax evaded, imprisonment up to 5 years. Civil penalties: 50% of the tax evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners may be personally liable for unpaid taxes and penalties if they knowingly participated in evasion. Travel bans and asset freezes may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Partnership has no real business activity, employees, or assets; used solely to shift profits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR may recharacterize transactions, disallow deductions, and impose penalties of 25% of the tax benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners may be personally liable for the tax benefit and penalties; limited partners may lose limited liability if they participate in management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML compliance measures (e.g., client identification, recordkeeping) as required by FINTRAC
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1 million for individuals and CAD 2 million for entities; criminal penalties for money laundering up to 10 years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be personally liable for AML violations if they knowingly participate in non-compliance.
